title: Trim control plane row width by extracting tenant blobs and introducing per-tenant query profiles
creator: Maya Thompson
description: The control plane tables (notably projects, tenants, and tenant_metadata) have grown wide due to large JSONB blobs and ad-hoc columns added over years. This increases IO, cache pressure, and slows planner decisions for our most common control-plane queries. This ticket reduces row width by extracting rarely-read JSON blobs into a compact shadow store and introduces a lightweight per-tenant query profile system to prioritize backfills and indexes for active tenants.
rationale: Shrinking row width reduces network IO and improves index cache residency. Per-tenant query profiles let us focus expensive backfills and index investments on tenants that drive hot queries (improving 95th/99th percentile latencies without a global heavy migration). This balances cost and customer impact.
proposal_summary: 1) Introduce tenant_metadata_shadow table to hold large JSON blobs and mark original jsonb column nullable. 2) Implement shadow-write pattern: application continues writing to jsonb and shadow table simultaneously during migration window. 3) Create a per-tenant query_profile table that captures query heat and a small set of inferred index hints. 4) Materialize a compact hot-join view (materialized view) for the most common join between tenant_metadata and tenant_users for active tenants. 5) Backfill shadow table and selectively materialize views for top X% tenants based on profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Row width of tenant table reduced by >= 40% for top 80% of tenants by row count after backfill
99th percentile latency for tenant read path reduced by >= 25% under production-like workload
Shadow-write tested for >= 48h with automatic fallback and no data loss observed
Per-tenant query_profile exposes heat metric and is consumed by backfill planner
Migration playbook and rollback steps documented in Confluence and reviewed by DB guild
migration_steps: Add tenant_metadata_shadow table with compact columns (tenant_id, blob_id, compressed_payload, last_seen_at)
Deploy application sidecar change to perform shadow-write to tenant_metadata_shadow alongside existing jsonb writes
Run incremental backfill job ordered by per-tenant query heat; throttle with rate limiter and circuit breaker
Swap reads: route low-risk reads to shadow table for tenants that have completed backfill; keep feature flag for gradual flip
Drop or set jsonb column to NULL via online schema change once majority of hot tenants migrated; schedule full cleanup outside peak hours
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: feature flag controlled shadow-write -> run backfill for top 5% tenants -> flip reads for those tenants -> expand to 20% -> monitor telemetry dashboards (p95/p99, replica lag, write amplification) -> proceed to remaining tenants in waves. Full cleanup scheduled in a maintenance window after telemetry stabilizes for 2 weeks.
performance_targets: Reduce average row size for tenant table by 40% for migrated tenants
Keep additional write amplification during shadow-write below 8%
testing_plan: Unit tests for shadow-write logic and fallback
Integration tests exercising read routing for mixed migrated/non-migrated tenants
Load test using production-sampled traces to verify p95/p99 improvements and backfill throttling behavior
Chaos test: simulate partial backfill interruption and verify automatic retry/resume
Pre-production run of backfill on staging with full telemetry collection
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Backfill causing overload on DB -> Mitigation: rate-limited backfill worker, adaptive throttle based on CPU and replica lag
Risk: Divergence between jsonb and shadow store during migration -> Mitigation: shadow-write ensures writes are duplicated; introduce consistency checker and reconcile job
Risk: Query planner regression after schema changes -> Mitigation: capture explain plans before/after and use per-tenant hints to guide index creation; roll back read flip if regressions observed
Risk: Long tail tenants without enough traffic get left in jsonb -> Mitigation: schedule low-priority background backfill for cold tenants during maintenance windows
